title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: KMP
tiers.description: The Non-executive Directors of the Company and its officeholders provided by the Manager (Argo Service Company Pty Ltd) under the Management Agreement, currently the Managing Director, the Chief Financial Officer and the Company Secretary.

definitions.hedging_definition: a transaction or arrangement to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company

windows.start_anchor: close of business on the last business day of the Company's half financial year
windows.end_anchor: the business day the Company's half-year financial results are announced to the ASX (inclusive)

windows.start_anchor: close of business on the last business day of the Company's full financial year
windows.end_anchor: the business day the Company's full-year financial results are announced to the ASX (inclusive)

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may from time to time impose additional prohibited periods if it is considering matters subject to ASX Listing Rule 3.1A (e.g. incomplete negotiations regarding a confidential proposal), and while it has orders in the market for its own securities (e.g. an on-market buy-back). The Company Secretary advises KMP when an additional prohibited period is imposed, but the underlying reason need not be disclosed.

rules.detail: A put and call over the Company's securities is a 'transaction or arrangement to limit the economic risk' of a security holding, i.e. hedging; hedging of unvested securities is prohibited outright.
rules.evidence: The Company prohibits hedging of any unvested securities.

rules.detail: Over vested securities, a derivative that limits economic risk requires the same approval as an ordinary trade: email approval from the Chairman, Managing Director and Company Secretary, valid 5 trading days, outside prohibited periods and without inside information. No stricter, hedging-specific regime applies.
rules.evidence: Any KMP seeking to enter a transaction or arrangement to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company must obtain approval in the same way as if they traded in the underlying securities direct.

rules.detail: Absolute prohibition on hedging any unvested securities; no vesting-state carve-out or clearance route.
rules.evidence: The Company prohibits hedging of any unvested securities.

rules.detail: Hedging of vested securities is permitted subject to obtaining the same approval as an ordinary trade under clause 5.
rules.evidence: Any KMP seeking to enter a transaction or arrangement to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company must obtain approval in the same way as if they traded in the underlying securities direct.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar structure over unvested securities operates to limit economic risk and is therefore banned hedging.
rules.evidence: The Company prohibits hedging of any unvested securities.

rules.detail: A monetisation arrangement over vested securities is an agreement to dispose of securities (Trading) and/or a risk-limiting arrangement (hedging); both require the standard clause 5 approval.
rules.evidence: entering into an agreement to apply for, acquire or dispose of, securities

rules.detail: Short selling is not named or referenced anywhere in the policy.
Securities lending is not named or referenced anywhere in the policy.
CFDs are not named. 'Securities' includes 'other derivatives of the Company's shares', so a CFD used to limit economic risk over unvested securities is caught by the hedging ban.
rules.evidence: The Company prohibits hedging of any unvested securities.

rules.detail: A CFD over vested securities used to limit economic risk requires the standard clause 5 approval, like any other hedging transaction.
rules.evidence: Any KMP seeking to enter a transaction or arrangement to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company must obtain approval in the same way as if they traded in the underlying securities direct.

rules.detail: No prior clearance is required to enter a loan facility secured on Company securities; the KMP must notify the Chairman (or Chair of Audit & Risk Committee if the KMP is Chairman) after entering the arrangement so the Board can assess materiality, potentially leading to market disclosure of key terms.
rules.evidence: Where a KMP has entered into an agreement where Company securities are held as collateral for a loan facility, the KMP must notify the Chairman (or in the case of the Chairman, the Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee) in order that the Board can ascertain whether the arrangement is material and if so, the Company will disclose the key terms of the arrangement to the market pursuant to the ASX continuous disclosure requirements.

rules.detail: Holding Company securities as collateral for a loan facility is expressly permitted, subject only to post-entry notification to the Chairman for materiality assessment; it is not itself a restricted 'Trading' event requiring prior approval.
rules.evidence: Where a KMP has entered into an agreement where Company securities are held as collateral for a loan facility, the KMP must notify the Chairman...

rules.detail: Any loan facility secured by Company securities is permitted with post-entry notification only (no prior approval, no prohibition), and a secured lender's disposal of the securities on enforcement is separately excluded from the policy altogether (clause 10).
rules.evidence: Where a KMP has entered into an agreement where Company securities are held as collateral for a loan facility, the KMP must notify the Chairman (or in the case of the Chairman, the Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee) in order that the Board can ascertain whether the arrangement is material...

rules.detail: No minimum holding period or restriction on short-term/frequent trading is stated.

clearance.approver: approval group: Chairman, Managing Director and Company Secretary
clearance.evidence: During non-prohibited periods, KMP must request approval to trade in ALI securities by email to the approval group comprising the Chairman, Managing Director and Company Secretary. Approvals to trade will remain valid for five trading days unless withdrawn during that period.

clearance.approver: approval group: Chairman, Chair of Audit & Risk Committee, Managing Director and Company Secretary
clearance.evidence: KMP must request approval to trade in exceptional circumstances by email to the approval group comprising the Chairman, Chair of Audit & Risk Committee, Managing Director and Company Secretary.

exceptions.evidence: transfers of securities already held by KMP into a superannuation fund or other entity in which KMP are a beneficiary

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme or arrangement (other than a scheme only investing in the Company's securities) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party

where a KMP is a trustee, trading in securities by that trust, provided the KMP is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decisions to trade during a prohibited period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the KMP
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer

accepting an offer or invitation made to all or some of the security holders, such as a rights issue, a share purchase plan, a dividend reinvestment plan, an equal access share buy-back, or an employee share plan
bona fide gifts of securities to a KMP by a third party or a transfer to a KMP under the terms of a will
where the beneficial interest in the relevant securities does not change
transactions conducted between a KMP and their spouse, civil partner, child, step-child, or other close family members
disposal of securities by a secured lender under a loan agreement secured by the securities

exceptions.approver: approval group: Chairman, Chair of Audit & Risk Committee, Managing Director and Company Secretary
exceptions.evidence: A KMP may be in severe financial difficulty if they have a pressing financial commitment that cannot be satisfied otherwise than by selling the Company's securities.

exceptions.approver: approval group: Chairman, Chair of Audit & Risk Committee, Managing Director and Company Secretary
exceptions.evidence: A circumstance will be considered exceptional if the KMP in question is required by a court order to transfer or sell the Company's securities or there is some other overriding legal requirement for them to do so.

financing_disclosure: KMP; trigger: entry into any agreement under which Company securities are held as collateral for a loan facility; to: the Chairman (or the Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee if the KMP is the Chairman); deadline: not specified. If the Board determines the arrangement is material, the Company discloses its key terms to the market under ASX continuous disclosure requirements.

exemption_authority: The approval group (Chairman, Managing Director and Company Secretary) approves trading in non-prohibited periods. For exceptional circumstances (severe financial difficulty, a court order, or another overriding legal requirement) a wider approval group (adding the Chair of Audit & Risk Committee) may clear a sale only, never a purchase, provided the KMP holds no inside information; the Company may need to notify the ASX of the existence of exceptional circumstances if such a trade proceeds.

bespoke_clauses.clause: disposal of securities by a secured lender under a loan agreement secured by the securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares on default is excluded from the policy altogether, so it is not restricted by prohibited periods or subject to any approval requirement — materially more favourable than most ASX trading policies.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where a KMP has entered into an agreement where Company securities are held as collateral for a loan facility, the KMP must notify the Chairman ... in order that the Board can ascertain whether the arrangement is material and if so, the Company will disclose the key terms of the arrangement to the market.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entering the secured loan leg of a funded collar requires no prior clearance at all, only post-entry notification for a materiality assessment, which could nonetheless result in the collar's key financing terms being disclosed to the market.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging approval equated to trading approval
bespoke_clauses.clause: Any KMP seeking to enter a transaction or arrangement to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company must obtain approval in the same way as if they traded in the underlying securities direct.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put/call overlay of a collar is treated identically to an ordinary share trade for approval purposes (same approval group, five-trading-day validity), not subject to any separate or stricter hedging regime.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company prohibits hedging of any unvested securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar cannot be written over unvested equity incentive holdings, but faces no hedging-specific restriction (beyond ordinary trade approval) once vested.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any trades resulting from approval must be immediately reported by the KMP to the approval group.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Execution of any collar leg or unwind must be reported immediately to the Chairman/Managing Director/Company Secretary group.

summary: A funded collar appears achievable under this policy, more so than under most ASX trading policies reviewed. Clause 7 treats a purchased put and written call as a hedging 'transaction or arrangement to limit economic risk', requiring only the same approval as an ordinary trade (email approval from the Chairman, Managing Director and Company Secretary, valid five trading days) once the underlying shares are vested; hedging of unvested securities alone is prohibited. The loan leg is treated even more favourably: clause 8 requires no prior approval to enter a loan facility secured on the shares, only post-entry notification to the Chairman for a Board materiality assessment (which may trigger market disclosure of the arrangement's key terms), and a secured lender's enforcement sale on default is expressly excluded from the policy altogether, avoiding any blackout-period conflict. Entry, rolls and unwind of the collar must still sit outside the half-year/full-year results blackout and any additional Company-imposed prohibited period, must not be undertaken while in possession of inside information, and any executed trade must be reported immediately to the approval group. Overall, both legs of a funded collar over vested ALI shares look implementable, subject to routine approval, a possible market disclosure of the financing terms if material, and timing outside blackout windows.
